text:
Lina: Noticed weird attribution on the schema dashboard. A bunch of fncall rejects in the strict-canary are showing up against the noop-tool route and losing the enforcement label.

Omar: Can you paste an example? is it the enum mismatch one we saw yesterday?

Lina: Yep. Validator logs show `validator.failure=missing_enum` and enforcement=strict-canary. Router moves to `noop_tool` as fallback. In the raw service log the request has labels: deployment=strict-canary, canary=true. But in the ingestion events the labels are gone and the route dimension is `noop_tool` so panels show it as normal-errors.

Priya: That's bad for quota and SLA math. If enforcement drops we undercount strict-canary rejects and our canary health check will look fine when it's not.

Ravi: I dug into the router code. When we rewrite the request during fallback we create a fresh telemetry envelope and only copy `route_id` and `model`. Old labels like `deployment` are not carried over. It was intentional to shrink envelope size but this edge-case is causing misattribution.

Lina: Maybe we should carry a tiny preserved label set for observability. We don't need the whole envelope.

Omar: Agree. Proposal: add preserved_labels header that includes only ["deployment","canary","enforcement"]. Router will attach preserved_labels BEFORE it mutates the route. Ingest will merge preserved_labels into the final event on pipeline entry.

Priya: Also update the console to surface `preserved_labels` on the reject flyout so SREs can see original enforcement. Right now the reject drilldown only shows final route and validator reason.

Ravi: Implementation note: preserved_labels should be base64-encoded JSON to avoid breaking existing header parsers. Keep the encoded blob under 1kb.

ingest-bot: Ingest pipeline v2 deployed 2025-01-03T11:08:21Z - now supports preserved_labels merge.

Omar: We should also adjust alerting. Canary health alerts currently check `schema.reject.rate{canary=true}` which assumes label survived. Until fix is live, add a temporary metric: `schema.reject.via_route{route=noop_tool,orig_enforcement=strict-canary}` via new parsing job.

Lina: I'll file the router PR and include a unit test that asserts preserved_labels are set on fallback. Will link to console change request too.

Priya: QA reminder: test that quota accounting still attributes charge to the original route if enforcement=strict. We bill differently for strict rejections (no token charge).

Ravi: For backfill we can run a pipeline job that joins logs with request traces to tag historical noop_tool rejects with inferred deployment where trace contains `deployment=strict-canary`. Low priority.

Omar: Timeline: router change + ingest merge -> canary health restored in next deploy window (48h). Console and backfill follow-ups planned for next sprint.

Lina: Thanks. I'll add a low-severity dashboard alert that fires if percentage of noop_tool rejects with missing preserved_labels > 0.5% per minute. No pager.

Priya: Sounds good. Also add an analytics event when preserved_labels are present so we can monitor overhead (event size).

Ravi: Will review PR. Ping me when CI green.
